subject: Request: Short-term SLO carve-in for Pacific maintenance window
messages:
From: James Liu <james.liu@quantiva.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Quantiva Procurement <procurement@quantiva.io>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Short-term SLO carve-in request for Pacific maintenance window

Hi Karthik,

Following up from our outage simulation last Friday — we need a short-term amendment to the P1/P2 response SLOs during a scheduled maintenance window in APAC. The maintenance is planned for 2027-06-10 22:00 to 2027-06-11 04:00 PT (overnight for your US ops). During that 6-hour window Quantiva will run an internal batch that will temporarily increase request volume and we'd like to avoid automated failover that would impact our data pipeline.

Request: carve-in a partial SLO exception so that Redwood keeps the primary routing to the dedicated pool (avoid region failover) and accepts a temporary increase in 95th percentile latency for P2s to 6 hours instead of standard 30 minutes. We understand this is an exception and are open to compensation/credits or stricter guardrails.

Action items from us: procurement needs any paperwork and an updated SLA amendment to sign. Operationally we can provide engineers on-call during that window and will pay for any surge capacity needed.

Can you confirm if Redwood can approve a short-term carve-in and what information you need?

Thanks,
James Liu
VP, Platform Ops
Quantiva Analytics

Attachments: maintenance_plan_q3.pdf (attached)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: James Liu <james.liu@quantiva.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term SLO carve-in request for Pacific maintenance window

James — thanks for the clear note and the heads-up. We can consider a controlled carve-in for that maintenance window but need to lock down technical guardrails, approval from the Support leadership, and a short mutual action plan (MAP) that covers:

- Exact start/end timestamps in UTC and which customer routes should be excluded from automated failover.
- A limited definition of P2 vs P1 for the window and confirmation that Quantiva will provide an on-call engineer reachable on Slack/phone.
- Agreed rollback criteria if error rates or 99th latency exceed thresholds.
- Any procurement/DocuSign paperwork to formalize the exception and credits.

Ben — can you and Soojin validate that our Dedicated pool can be pinned for a 6-hr carve-in without violating other customers' capacity SLAs? If so, we should prepare a short runbook and a temporary escalation path (support->oncall->ops lead->engineering manager).

James — if you can send the maintenance window in UTC and an engineer contact, I'll kick off the internal approval and send a draft SLO amendment for procurement.

— Karthik
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term SLO carve-in request for Pacific maintenance window

Quick internal note — I checked capacity and we can support a 6-hour carve-in for Quantiva provided we put these constraints in place:

- Carve-in limited to their dedicated pool only (no cross-customer resource sharing).
- Temporary P2 latency SLO relaxed to a max of 6 hours for this window; P1 response must remain at standard escalation (we'll treat any P1 as normal).
- Quantiva must activate an on-call engineer and join the incident bridge at the start of the window.
- We require an automatic fallback to cross-region routing if error rate for the dedicated pool > 5% sustained for 5 minutes.

I'll draft a short runbook and roster change (attached) and send to procurement for an SLA amendment. Soojin — can you confirm the routing guard implementation and whether we need an emergency capacity buffer?

Attachments: oncall-shift-roster.xlsx

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Support Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: James Liu <james.liu@quantiva.io>, Quantiva Procurement <procurement@quantiva.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term SLO carve-in request for Pacific maintenance window

James — confirmed. We have the internal approval to proceed with a temporary SLO carve-in for the window you specified, subject to the MAP below. Procurement: please review the attached SLO_change_proposal.pdf and confirm whether a short DocuSign amendment is sufficient.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — agreed items:
1) Window (UTC): 2027-06-11 05:00 to 2027-06-11 11:00 UTC (aligns with your proposed PT times).
2) Scope: Dedicated pool pinned for Quantiva routes only; no region failover unless error-rate threshold exceeded (5% sustained > 5 minutes).
3) P1 handling: normal P1 escalation (15-minute response target). P2 handling: relaxed to 6 hours only within the defined window.
4) On-call: Quantiva to provide an engineer on the bridge; Redwood on-call responder will be the primary contact.
5) Runbook & rollback: Ben will circulate a 2-page runbook and the on-call roster (attached).
6) Billing/credits: if we take measurable customer-impactable risk, we will apply a one-time administrative credit; procurement to confirm.
7) Post-window review: Joint postmortem within 72 hours if any deviations occur.

Next steps (owner):
- Quantiva: confirm engineer contact and sign DocuSign (Quantiva Procurement).
- Ben: share runbook and enable routing guard.
- Soojin: validate routing guard and emergency buffer.
- Karthik/Marissa: finalize SLO amendment language for procurement.

Thanks everyone — I'll schedule a 15-min sync before the window and share the bridge link.

— Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Related links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUPPORT-3245 (runbook ticket)
Attachments: SLO_change_proposal.pdf, oncall-shift-roster.xlsx
